profile.address: 32 Avenue of the Americas, Tribeca, New York, NY 10013
profile.reading: Per the English Wikipedia article on 32 Avenue of the Americas, this Tribeca, Manhattan building (also known as 32 Sixth Avenue, ZIP 10013) totals 1.17 million square feet of office space (800,000 sq ft when it first opened as rentable space). Built in three phases from 1914 through 1932 as the AT&T Long Distance Building, it was designated a New York City landmark in 1991 and renovated 2001 to 2002. The 24th floor houses The Hub, a carrier neutral colocation and interconnection facility serving over 50 terrestrial carriers, content providers, ISPs, and enterprise tenants.
profile.capacity_note: Colocation and interconnection facility (The Hub) occupies the 24th floor of a larger mixed use office building; no MW figure published

reading.body:
The Hub occupies a single floor of a 1.17 million square foot Manhattan office building originally constructed for AT&T between 1914 and 1932. It functions as a carrier-neutral colocation and interconnection point serving over 50 network operators, content providers, and enterprise customers. No power capacity is published for the facility.

New York has only one data center with published power specifications in this database, totaling 3 MW. This campus ranks second by published capacity in the state, though that ranking reflects the absence of published figures rather than measured scale. The state has 31 mapped facilities overall, the vast majority of which disclose no power draw.

The facility qualifies for colocation and terrestrial carrier interconnection. Whether the Hub's IT load can support meaningful AI workloads depends on figures not published, including floor-level power allocation, cooling capacity, and current occupancy. Tribeca location and landmark designation impose constraints on physical expansion that are not quantified here.
